   STAFF REPORT

Meeting Date:  January 4, 2024
To:  Honorable Mayor & Council Member Friedman
From:  Joana Torres, Community Services Manager
Subject:  Beverly Hills Community Dog Park
Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
In September 2019, the Recreation and Parks Commission reviewed several surface
options that were considered during the design phase of the dog park. The Commission
also provided additional surface options for the park based on research comprised of 18
parks in the surrounding areas. The goal was to gather their feedback and present it to
the City Council Liaisons for further direction. However, due to the pandemic this project
was placed on hold. This year the Recreation and Parks commission has received public
comments and concerns about the surface of the park and the desire to replace it.
DISCUSSION
The Recreation and Parks Commission was presented with the following findings in
2019:
- Grass
Based on research, grass was proven to be hard to maintain in other dog parks due to
the wear and tear from the dogs running, digging, and urinating. Due to the daily impact
from dogs, parks with natural grass close for a period of time for reseeding and
maintenance. This would be an inconvenience to the patrons that use the park as part of
their dog’s regular exercise routine.

- Artificial Turf
Quotes to install and maintain the dog park with artificial turf were much more expensive
compared to the current decomposed granite. The cost to maintain artificial turf is higher
due to the frequency in which it must be washed down to eliminate odors. The need to
wash the turf during a period of severe drought conditions became an increasing
concern during the surface discussion. Additionally, there were also concerns about the
temperature of the artificial turf during the summer months with so much of the park
being exposed to the sun. In October 2023, Governor Gavin Newsom passed legislation
allowing cities to ban artificial turf due to its potential health concerns. Staff will work with
the City’s Project Administration team in gathering information and researching the
potential risks if the Liaisons decide to move forward with artificial turf.
 Meeting Date: January 4, 2024
- Woodchips/Bark
Small insects and bugs tend to live in this material and could possibly cause harm to the
dogs. Abrasions to the dogs’ paws was also a concern.

- Wood Fiber
Engineered Wood Fiber is made from virgin wood fibers that have been screened to
yield particles that generally do not exceed ½″ x 2″ in size and there were concerns of
dogs ingesting them.

- Stone Dust
This does not drain well and is best used on gently sloping pavement surfaces, as it can
be disturbed by constant traffic.

- Pea Stone
This product is subject to movement, when disturbed, due to the roundness of the stone
particles.

- Mulch
Material needs to be replaced and refreshed periodically to prevent urine saturation in
the mulch. This proves to also have similar concerns to the bark/woodchips that was
discussed previously.

- Rice Stone
Processed stone material, the range in gradation size helps to reduce the movement of
the stone particles when disturbed through dog activity.
Commissioners directed staff to investigate alternate surface options that included a
combination of mixed materials that would be both aesthetically appealing and
functional. The Commission also suggested allowing the opportunity for dog park
patrons to provide their feedback on surface options through a Town Hall meeting.

At a December 2019 liaison meeting, staff presented the Commission’s requests to City
Council Liaisons, Vice Mayor Lester Friedman and Councilmember Julian Gold, MD. At
that time, a permanent shade structure was considered a priority since the 11 trees
planted had not matured. Staff were also directed to come forward with additional
research on surfaces and costs in early 2020. However, due to the Covid-19 pandemic,
this item had been tabled.
Currently the shade structure is being designed through Project Administration as part of
the 2024 fiscal year Capital Improvement Project. The Recreation and Parks
Commission has recommended bringing forward the request to replace the ground
covering at the dog park.
FISCAL IMPACT
No fiscal impact at this time.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff is seeking City Council Liaison’s recommendation regarding the current surface of
the Beverly Hills Dog Park as well as direction on surveying the public for feedback
regarding the park.

  Joana Torres,
  Community Services Manager
  Approved By

CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison/Recreation and Parks Commission Committee

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Thursday, January 04, 2024
  4:30 PM

4MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 04, 2024 / 4:30 PM

IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Gold; Vice Mayor Lester Friedman; Nancy Hunt-Coffey, City
  Manager; Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services; Patty Acuna,
  Assistant Director of Community Services; Mandana Motahari, City
  Architect; Joana Torres, Community Services Manager; Matthew Brown,
  Recreation Services Manager; Recreation and Parks Commission Chair
  Amie Sherry, Recreation and Parks Commissioner JR Dzubak; Linda
  Kyriazi, Management Assistant.

1)  PUBLIC COMMENT

  a) Members of the public will be given the opportunity to directly address the
  Committee on any item listed on the agenda.

  Speakers:  None

  2) Request from Recreation and Parks Commission to revisit Community Dog Park
  Resurfacing
  Joana Torres, Community Services Manager, provided the history of surface options that
  were considered during the design phase of the Dog Park. The Recreation and Parks
  Commission has received public comments and concerns about the surface of the Dog
  Park and the desire to replace it.

  Staff is seeking support of the City Council Liaisons to continue research on surface
  options as well as surveying the public for feedback.

  Chair Amie Sherry, Recreation and Parks Commission, informed the Liaisons on the
  public comment complaints the Commission has received on the Dog Park surface. The
  decomposed granite that is currently being used provides a lot of dust on the dog. It was
  suggested to integrate a variety of materials that would be safe for the dog in addition to
  further investigate the options to see if there have been any updates since the prior seven
  years research.

  Commissioner Dzubak commented on the decline in numbers patronizing the Dog Park
  which is an assumption on attendees complaints.
 Beverly Hills City Council Liaison/Recreation and Parks Commission
January 04, 2024
Special Meeting Highlights

  Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services, updated the Liaisons on the shade
  structure which was previously approved to move forward and is part of the City’s Capital
  Improvement Budget. The City’s Architect has completed design specs and those will be
  presented to the Commission. The original new trees that were placed now have matured
  and provide canopies for shade.

  Mayor Gold supported receiving feedback from the public but stressed that a significant
  number of participants is needed. As far as artificial turf, change for the sake of change
  is not necessarily a good thing especially at a significant cost. Mayor Gold additionally
  suggested staff compare and contrast any alternative surfaces both in terms of
  advantages and disadvantages, its cost to implement in addition to the cost to maintain.
  Staff is to make sure the study is a robust one.

  Vice Chair Friedman concurred with Mayor Gold that possibly not much change has
  happened to Dog Park turf in the seven years from conception but supports staff
  researching.

  Next Steps: A survey will be conducted to Dog Park users in addition to other marketing
  so potential Dog Park users can participate. The Ad Hoc will begin research on various
  components and will return to the Liaisons with findings along with potential
  recommendations.

  Nancy Hunt-Coffey, City Manager, suggested adding some broad-based questions to the
  survey related to the surfacing along with shading and park access to see if there are
  other deterrents in non-participation.

3)  ADJOURNMENT
  Date / Time: January 04, 2024 / 5:07 PM
